title: Federal Judge Refuses to Order Texas to Extradite Charged ICE Agent Christian Castro
excerpt: A federal district judge in Texas declined to order Gov. Greg Abbott to extradite ICE agent Christian Castro to Minnesota, where he faces felony assault and false-reporting charges for the January shooting of Julio Sosa-Celis. The ruling paved the way for Castro's release the following day.
content:
On August 26, 2026, U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. of the Southern District of Texas denied Minnesota's request to compel Texas Governor Greg Abbott to facilitate the extradition of ICE agent Christian Castro, who has been charged in Minnesota with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime.

Judge Rodriguez wrote that he lacked the authority to prevent the Cameron County sheriff from releasing Castro, or to order the Texas governor to sign his extradition warrant. The ruling reflected a determination that the governor had not violated federal law by refusing to extradite.

  • Castro had been in Texas custody since May 29, 2026, when he was arrested by the Texas Rangers on a nationwide warrant issued by a Minnesota judge.
  • Minnesota sought his extradition in connection with the January 14, 2026 shooting of 24-year-old Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis during Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis.
  • Prosecutors allege Castro fired through the front door of a Minneapolis home, hitting Sosa-Celis in the leg, and then falsely accused the victim and another man of attacking officers with a broom and snow shovel — allegations later disproven by video evidence.
  • Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison had sued Governor Abbott to force the extradition; the lawsuit did not succeed in time.

The ruling illustrated a growing accountability gap in which state criminal charges against federal immigration agents face structural obstacles to enforcement when states with different political alignments become involved.
